targets.body_template: ### Assay context **Experimenter-confirmed mapping correction.** The construct labels below supersede the earlier Test 2 labels. The source wells, RFU readings and endpoint calculations are unchanged; column 12 is Blank, whose composition is not documented. This is a relabelling of the same acquisition, not an independent experiment. Test 2 measures **the Or35a+ORCO co-expression condition associated with this receptor module** across six additions, mapped to **column 10**. The condition label links the measurements to the team's expression system; it does not independently confirm the clone sequence or membrane localization. This is a system-level observation, not an independent assay of a bare CDS or isolated reporter domain. The supplied preparation is 1:1,000 odorant dilution, 1:100 VUAA1 dilution and 0.1% DMSO. Stock molarities and the underlying formulation are not independently recoverable from the exports. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) give the full construct/stimulus mapping, calculation and provenance. ### Test 2: corrected changes and VUAA1-referenced responses ![Or35a: Test 2 corrected changes S and construct-matched VUAA1 reference ratios N](REGISTRY_IMAGE_UPLOAD_OR35A) *Upper panel: S = ΔF1 − ΔF0, in percentage points (pp), using the observed F1 change over 168 s and F0 change over 48 s. Lower panel: N = (S − DMSO S) / (VUAA1 S − DMSO S), the same dimensionless normalization used in the Results heatmap. DMSO is 0 and VUAA1 is 1 by definition; these anchors do not bound other responses. Negative values remain visible. Each condition–addition pair is one separate well.* ΔF0 = 100 × (last F0 / first F0 − 1); ΔF1 = 100 × (last F1 / first F1 − 1). **S = ΔF1 − ΔF0**, in percentage points (pp). S48 repeats the calculation using only the first 48 s of F1 and the full 48 s of F0; it is a window sensitivity check, not an extra replicate. The separate DMSO-well contrast is shown alongside S rather than replacing it. | Well | Addition | ΔF0 (%) · 48 s | ΔF1 (%) · 168 s | S (pp) | S − vehicle S (pp) | S48 (pp) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A10 | VUAA1 | -2.68 | +26.78 | +29.46 | +30.83 | +9.82 | | D10 | Isopentyl acetate | -1.45 | -2.45 | -1.00 | +0.37 | +0.28 | | E10 | 2-Heptanone | -1.18 | -1.91 | -0.74 | +0.63 | +0.41 | | F10 | Valeric acid | -0.92 | +0.89 | +1.81 | +3.18 | +1.08 | | G10 | Pentyl acetate | -1.64 | -2.00 | -0.36 | +1.00 | +0.66 | | H10 | DMSO vehicle | -1.11 | -2.48 | -1.37 | +0.00 | +0.31 | ### Interpretation **Reading S and N together.** For this construct, VUAA1 has **S = +29.46 pp** and the separate DMSO well has **S = -1.37 pp**. Their difference is **+30.83 pp**, so the VUAA1 ratio is **N = 1.000**. The value 1 in the Results heatmap is this reference ratio, not a corrected change of 1 pp. The bars, the accompanying table and the heatmap use the same Test 2 endpoints; no response values were changed to produce this display. For VUAA1, the within-F1 change is **+26.78%**, while F0 changes **-2.68%**. Their disturbance-corrected contrast is **S = +29.46 pp**. The DMSO well has **S = -1.37 pp**, giving a separate vehicle difference of **+30.83 pp**. The matched-duration sensitivity value for VUAA1 is **S48 = +9.82 pp**. S answers whether the recorded F1 trajectory changes more than the recorded F0 trajectory. It does not compare the absolute mean F1 level with the preceding mean F0 level. Those acquisitions can begin at different fluorescence levels, so a rising F1 trace and a lower F1 mean are compatible. The earlier mean-ratio calculation remains in the historical audit summary (retained in the source archive with its superseded labels) and is not the primary response measure here. The two windows differ in duration (168 s versus 48 s), so S is not a matched-duration rate correction. This screen contains one observed well per condition–addition pair; repeated readings do not supply independent cultures. Positive S means F1 changes more, or decreases less, than F0; it need not imply a raw F1 increase. It is not proof of receptor-specific activation, calcium influx, selectivity or a detection limit. Negative values are not classified as inhibition. The [exploratory VUAA1-referenced supplement](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-vuaa1-reference) rescales the separate odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts by this condition's VUAA1-minus-DMSO contrast, **+30.83 pp**. It retains the S values above and does not measure or correct per-well transfection efficiency. ### F1-only dynamic reanalysis A separate reanalysis of the retained F1 readings uses the supplied F1 workbook channel labels and source-cell map. For **Or35a**, the odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts are **2-heptanone: +0.62 pp; isopentyl acetate: +0.12 pp; valeric acid: +2.98 pp; pentyl acetate: +0.48 pp**. Each well is normalized to its first-three-reading mean; the contrast subtracts the matched channel’s DMSO late-to-early change from the odorant change (last-three mean / first-three mean − 1). This metric uses F1 only and is distinct from S and VUAA1-referenced N above; it does not replace those calculations or supply an independent biological replicate. VUAA1 is retained as reference data without division or threshold selection. One well represents each condition. A positive contrast can reflect less decline than DMSO; it does not establish receptor-specific activation. The experimenter confirmed this F1 channel mapping; it supersedes the earlier Test 2 receptor labels, without changing the raw measurements. [Full F1/DoOR comparison and interpretation](https://2026.igem.wiki/nthu/results#f1-dynamic-door) · [Analysis and validation source](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/nthu/aerosense/-/tree/main/code/aerosense/wetlab/odor-f1-dynamic).

targets.title: Using the drift-adjusted profiles for the next experiment
targets.body_markdown:
The additional dataset contributes inspectable within-stage trajectories, a baseline-drift correction, explicitly supplied vehicle preparation and a complete construct map. The rising VUAA1 trajectories are represented by the corrected S statistic; their lower between-acquisition mean levels are retained as a different descriptive audit. Neither comparison should be used to erase the other or to infer an unrecorded injection transient.

Positive S is consistent with a fluorescence increase during F1 that exceeds the measured F0-stage drift. It does not isolate receptor-dependent calcium entry from other time-dependent cellular, chemical or optical effects. The unequal time windows, separate vehicle wells and absence of independent cultures limit causal interpretation. Inspect S48 and the entire traces before choosing the repeat experiment; repeat the relevant stimulus, vehicle, ORCO-only and blank controls (composition not documented) under documented fixed settings and timings.

The Test 1 four-acquisition metric and Test 2 two-acquisition metric stay distinct. The receptor coding sequences and individual fusion domains retain Design-only status, because all these measurements concern assembled expression conditions. Sequence confirmation, protein localization, dose dependence, selectivity and detection limits remain separate validation questions.

targets.title: Or67b coding sequence for assembly into an olfactory receptor expression system
targets.body_markdown:
### Intended role and assembly

Insect tuning receptors and Orco form heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. This CDS supplies the Or67b subunit. For this platform it is co-expressed with the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion `BBa_26E11Z80`; a response depends on the assembled system and the cellular context. The isolated sequence is not a complete sensing device.

Use this part to choose your own promoter, expression marker or fusion arrangement. The corresponding bicistronic module includes a GCCACC initiation context and IRES-mCherry. For either design, supply suitable transcriptional control and polyadenylation from the mammalian vector, and verify start/stop codons and reading frame against the actual assembled sequence. Expression, localization and channel function require separate checks.

### Functional architecture

![Or67b CDS in the expression-module context](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/fdb33183817b2d7006e8258973fcb0b0b9b10affd449c9d743b75f547fed6a67.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted Or67b CDS is the basic part; GCCACC initiation context, EMCV IRES and mCherry belong to the assembled expression module, not this isolated sequence. The calcium-reporter/Orco construct is a separate partner. The diagram does not assert experimental localization or activity.*

### Sequence provenance

| Item | Team design record |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Gene | [FBgn0036019](https://flybase.org/reports/FBgn0036019.html) |
| Transcript | FBtr0076420 |
| RefSeq protein | [NP_524007](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/protein/NP_524007) |
| Reference protein length | 421 amino acids |
| Production | Human codon-adapted DNA, synthesised by GenScript; used in a pcDNA3.1(+) expression context |

The intended protein is the native reference receptor; codon adaptation concerns the DNA design. These identifiers establish the design source, not sequence confirmation of every laboratory plasmid. Undigested gel migration and colony growth cannot verify this insert's identity. The submitted sequence and the experimental clone should be checked independently before reuse.

### Trace from this CDS to the tested condition

The corresponding [BBa_269VSDDR module](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-269vsddr) places this coding sequence upstream of IRES-mCherry. Its documentation shows the Or67b-labelled colony plate (photograph 3, upper-right), gel A lanes 3–4, the fixed-cell **Or67b+ORCO** condition and P2 **column 07**. These labels connect the design to the team's preparation records. They do not resolve which saved colony supplied each later assay or independently confirm the DNA sequence.

A user can therefore reuse the CDS design and inspect the module-level observations, while choosing a different transcriptional or reporter arrangement. Such a change should be characterized as a new expression context; neither mCherry brightness nor the fusion's calcium-associated fluorescence measures the abundance or activity of this isolated receptor protein.

### Evidence and limits

This bare CDS was not tested separately. Its composite module page contains the condition-specific microscopy counts and exploratory P2 fluorescence measurements. Those observations must not be counted again as an independent characterisation of this basic part, nor taken as proof of membrane localization or receptor specificity.

Codon adaptation was chosen to support mammalian expression. The stable-cell study by Zboray et al. provides relevant precedent [2], but the present records do not contain a matched wild-type-versus-adapted comparison. No improvement in expression or sensing can therefore be attributed to codon adaptation here.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **1,266 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **PstI×5; BsaI×1; BbsI×1**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

The published CDS includes an ATG start and terminal stop codon. Its promoter, initiation context and polyadenylation must be supplied appropriately for the intended expression system.

### References

1. Sato K, Pellegrino M, Nakagawa T, et al. Insect olfactory receptors are heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels. *Nature* 452, 1002–1006 (2008). https://doi.org/10.1038/nature06850
2. Zboray K, Toth AV, Miskolczi TD, et al. High-throughput ligand profile characterization in novel cell lines expressing seven heterologous insect olfactory receptors for the detection of volatile plant biomarkers. *Scientific Reports* 13, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4



### Additional system-level characterization

Test 2 maps **Or67b+ORCO to column 7**. The corresponding [BBa_269VSDDR module entry](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-269vsddr#odor-2026-10-21) gives the complete six-addition traces and within-F1 changes after subtraction of F0-stage drift. These measurements belong to the labelled co-expression condition. They do not independently characterize the bare CDS, verify receptor localization or establish a ligand-specific response. The Test 1 paired-round measurements retain their distinct definition and source mapping.
